pr_title: fetch: Add additional diagnostic output when a fetch fails in the FIPS provider.
pr_body:
The existing "fetch failed" message potentially buried in a big error stack was not very helpful.
This includes the algorithm and property query being used and unifies the code between the by name and by number fetch routines.

Fixes #12285
pr_comments:
> Instead of a generic error function, which not simply move the error recording into `inner_evp_generic_function`?

It seemed cleaner this way:
- a single error exit point instead of five
- the number or name dichotomy would complicate further

> a single error exit point instead of five

What's another goto?  ;-)

How about you hold on for a bit?  I actually have a branch [sic!] where I'm centralising the error reporting...  the twist for that branch is that it gives different error records if the algo was unavailable or if there was some other failure, such as memory allocation faults.

UPDATE: #12857
Different errors was a thought I had which would have justified putting the error handling in the internal function.
This is now incorporated in #12857.  Closing.

issue_context.title: Unhelpful error in for deprecated digest functions: "failed fetch"
comments: @jeroen thanks for taking the time to write such a detailed report and add a reproducer!

The fix to your immediate problem is to load the "legacy" provider using the `OSSL_PROVIDER_load()` call.  You'll also have to load the "default" provider using the same call to avoid some weird order dependent things happening.

As for the error message, we'll need to come up with something: the root cause is that the function `EVP_MD_fetch()` is failing.

Thanks for the report, as @mspncp noted, we really appreciate a good write up and reproduction code.

I have added the following to my code:

```c
  OSSL_PROVIDER_load(NULL, "legacy");   
  OSSL_PROVIDER_load(NULL, "default");
```

This fixed the failed fetch error, however now my TLS tests no longer seem to work. Do I need to load a special provider to enable networking?

Some API call to load a provider in addition to the default providers may be helpful :)

> As for the error message, we'll need to come up with something: the root cause is that the function `EVP_MD_fetch()` is failing.

Additional text saying what the possibilities are would be nice.  However, the caller must be willing to actually get that additional text, and `ERR_get_error()` is not the right function to get that.
I did some work related to this in #13467, where there's central detection if the algo to be fetched is unavailable, or if there was some other error.
Marking as inactive, to be closed at the end of 3.4 dev, barring further input

review_comments: This suggests something I've had in the back of my mind, that we should name the library contexts...

Me too ... with a named library context we get cross context functionality.  Pass the digest, property query and library context name to HMAC or digest sign instead of just the first two.

The additional name here isn't the important point, the first stab at it didn't name bother.  The algorithm and property queries are the important diagnostic.  Once I started refactoring common code, the name made sense.
